questions.question: There are many ideas about how the world will 'end'. Do you think the world will end some day? Have you ever thought what would happen if the sun got so hot that it 'burnt' the earth, or so cold that the earth became frozen?
answer_steps: Many scientists believe the world could end through heat from the sun or a frozen ice age.
Frost uses these ideas to talk about human emotions that can destroy the world.

questions.question: For Frost, what do 'fire' and 'ice' stand for? Choose from: greed, avarice, cruelty, lust, conflict, fury, intolerance, rigidity, insensitivity, coldness, indifference, hatred.
answer_steps: Fire: greed, avarice, lust, conflict, fury (desire).
Ice: cruelty, intolerance, rigidity, insensitivity, coldness, indifference, hatred.

questions.question: What is the rhyme scheme of the poem? How does it help in bringing out the contrasting ideas in the poem?
answer_steps: The rhyme scheme is aba abc bcb.
The rhymes tie 'fire' and 'ice' words together, so the poem swings between the two opposite ideas, both leading to destruction.

questions.question:
Read the extract and answer the questions.

*Some say the world will end in fire,*
*Some say in ice.*
*From what I've tasted of desire*
*I hold with those who favour fire.*

(i) Name the poem and the poet.

(ii) What does 'fire' symbolise?

(iii) Why does the poet favour fire?

(iv) What does 'I hold with' mean?

(v) Find the rhyming words.
answer_steps: (i) Fire and Ice, Robert Frost.
(ii) Desire: greed and lust.
(iii) From his own experience of desire.
(iv) I agree with.
(v) fire/desire/fire.

questions.question:
Read the extract and answer the questions.

*But if it had to perish twice,*
*I think I know enough of hate*
*To say that for destruction ice*
*Is also great*
*And would suffice.*

(i) What does 'it' refer to?

(ii) What does 'ice' stand for?

(iii) What does 'perish' mean?

(iv) What does 'suffice' mean?

(v) What is the poet's view of hatred?
answer_steps: (i) The world.
(ii) Hatred.
(iii) Be destroyed, die.
(iv) Be enough.
(v) It is powerful enough to destroy the world.

questions.question: Fire and Ice was written by:
questions.explanation: He also wrote Dust of Snow.

questions.question: The poet says he holds with those who favour:
questions.explanation: From what he has tasted of desire.
option_feedback: He favours fire, but says ice is also great.

questions.question: 'If it had to perish twice' means:
options: if the poet had to die twice
if the world had to be destroyed a second time

questions.explanation: Fire stands for desire; ice stands for hatred.
option_feedback: Not quite. Fire stands for desire; ice stands for hatred.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false: The poet believes ice would be enough to destroy the world.
questions.explanation: 'For destruction ice is also great and would suffice.'
option_feedback: Correct! 'For destruction ice is also great and would suffice.'
Not quite. 'For destruction ice is also great and would suffice.'

questions.question: How are 'fire' and 'ice' used to talk about human emotions? Which do you think is more dangerous today?
answer_steps: Fire stands for desire: greed, lust and ambition that spread fast and destroy.
Ice stands for hatred: coldness and indifference that destroy slowly.
Frost says either would be enough to end the world.
Today, greed harms nature through over-use of resources, while hatred causes wars and divides people.
Both must be controlled; the poem is a warning to humanity.
